name: Knott's Scary Farm
summary: Knott's Scary Farm is the oldest big haunt in the country — running since 1973 — and still among the best: dozens of mazes, scare zones through the real Ghost Town, and a separately-ticketed night event that transforms the whole park.
h1: Knott's Scary Farm: what it is, what it costs, and whether it is worth it
title: Knott's Scary Farm
description: Knott's Scary Farm, the original big Halloween haunt: mazes, Ghost Town scare zones and shows on a separate ticket. The honest worth-it verdict and the planning playbook.

pricing.cheapestNights: Thursday nights early in the season
pricing.priciestNights: The last two Saturdays before Halloween and Halloween night itself
notes: Line-skip products for the mazes are sold separately and price up sharply on peak nights.
Some passholder and early-buy discounts appear at announcement each year.

whatYouGet: A dozen or more full walk-through mazes — the count and quality that defined the genre and still leads it.
Scare zones through the real Ghost Town streets, which no other haunt can match for atmosphere.
Shows, street performers and the hanging-style spectacles the event is famous for.
Select rides running through the night, coaster lineup included.
whatYouDont: The family day park — Scary Farm is a separate night event, and the daytime park closes early on event nights.
Anything child-friendly after the gates: the event is uniformly intense and recommends against young guests.
All-you-can-maze access at the base ticket on peak nights — the queue math without a line-skip product on Saturdays is brutal.

verdict.short: Worth it, unambiguously, for any haunt fan — Scary Farm is the genre's founding event and still its benchmark. Buy a Thursday in late September and it is also the best-value haunt night in the country.
worthItIf: Halloween is your season and mazes are the product you travel for.
You can go on a weeknight early in the run — the crowd difference is the difference between ten mazes and five.
You want the atmosphere only a real ghost town can give a scare event.
skipIf: You dislike jump scares, fog, darkness or being touched-adjacent in tight spaces — intensity is the product.
Your only available night is a late-October Saturday and you will not buy the maze line-skip.
You are bringing anyone under the recommendation age — this is not a light-scare evening.

strategy.heading: The night you pick is the whole decision
body: A late-September Thursday and the Saturday before Halloween are different events sharing one name. The early weeknight runs calm enough to clear every maze once; the peak Saturday runs queues that make the line-skip product nearly mandatory. If your calendar flexes at all, buy the calmer night and buy it early — the best dates sell out.

strategy.heading: The maze order
body: The honest playbook: hit the new marquee mazes first — they hold the longest queues all night — then work the Ghost Town streets, then the back-lot mazes in the final hours when their lines thin. The event map publishes the maze list on announcement day; plan three targets before you arrive and treat everything else as the bonus it will feel like.

strategy.heading: Line-skip arithmetic, honestly
body: The maze line-skip product is expensive and, on peak nights, transforms the event — this is the rare upcharge this site recommends without hedging on those nights. On calm weeknights it is unnecessary; skip it and spend the difference on the photo pass. The decision is the night you chose, made twice.

food.note: Scary Farm food is event-branded and better than the day park's — the seasonal food booths concentrate near the Ghost Town edges and the Boardwalk.

items.name: Boysenberry items, haunt edition
items.verdict: The farm's signature berry in spooky packaging — the reliable snack between mazes.

faqs.q: Is Knott's Scary Farm included with day admission?
faqs.a: No. It is a separate hard-ticket night event, and the day park closes early on event nights to reset. Day admission and Scary Farm are two different products with two different crowds.

Genuinely intense — maze density, scare actors, fog and darkness at a level the regional Fright Fests do not attempt. The park itself warns against young guests, and this site endorses that warning: this is a produced haunt, not a decorated ride day.

Select nights from mid-September through Halloween night in the typical pattern — roughly 22 to 36 nights a season, Thursdays through Sundays. The current cycle's dates are on the park's event page; this site carries the pattern with a confidence label.

In the recent pattern, per-night tickets have run roughly $60 to $130 depending on the night, with opening-night and early-season discounts below that. Prices move by date; the park's ticketing page is the live number.

faqs.q: Is it the best haunt in the country?
faqs.a: It is the argument's center. Knott's invented the big-park haunt in 1973 and still leads on maze count and Ghost Town atmosphere; the Universal parks' Halloween Horror Nights lead on IP production. Haunt fans ride both and argue forever — this site's verdict is that Scary Farm on a calm night is the best value in the genre.
